t: Tate is the institution behind a network of four art galleries, which together hold the United Kingdom's national collection of British art, and international modern and contemporary art. It isn't a government body, though its main sponsor is the Department for Culture, Media and Sport. The name goes back to Sir Henry Tate, the sugar merchant and philanthropist who founded the Tate Gallery. He also established Henry Tate and Sons, which later became Tate and Lyle. The corporate body was set up under the Museums and Galleries Act 1992.
